# FALLBACK robots.txt — hostname-neutral on purpose.
#
# This file lives in the shared dist/ and is therefore served on EVERY city
# domain in the fleet. It previously carried two absolute Sitemap: lines and a
# canonical-host comment for one specific city, which meant every other city's
# crawlers were sent to another town's sitemap. A Sitemap: directive requires an
# absolute URL, and an absolute URL cannot be correct for more than one city —
# so the sitemap lines are gone from here entirely.
#
# The real, per-city robots.txt is generated by the serve-robots edge function
# (supabase/functions/serve-robots/index.ts). IT ONLY TAKES EFFECT ONCE THE
# HOSTING LAYER ROUTES  /robots.txt -> serve-robots  FOR EACH CITY DOMAIN
# (Netlify/Vercel/Cloudflare rewrite — the same mechanism serve-page needs).
# Until that rewrite is configured, this file is what crawlers get, and the
# sitemap must be submitted directly in Google Search Console / Bing Webmaster
# Tools instead. That is a deliberate trade: no sitemap hint beats a wrong one.
#
# Everything below is safe on any hostname.

# SINGLE-CITY PRAGMATISM — REMOVE BEFORE LAUNCHING CITY #2.
# The fleet-correct design serves robots.txt per city via the serve-robots edge
# function, and this static file stays hostname-neutral. But today exactly one
# city exists, the hosting rewrite is not configured yet, and a missing sitemap
# hint costs real discovery on the only live domain. So the absolute line below
# is correct for now and wrong the moment a second domain serves this file.
# When city #2 launches: delete these lines and wire /robots.txt -> serve-robots.
# Two sitemaps on purpose: the static one refreshes per build; the edge one is
# always current (cross-host Sitemap: references are valid from robots.txt).
Sitemap: https://lakegenevabrief.com/sitemap.xml
Sitemap: https://mzumvkrpnxhkvhdyzgqa.supabase.co/functions/v1/serve-sitemap?city_id=default
